name: judge
description: Reviews a frozen software candidate, such as a branch, diff or pull request, for acceptance. Use when testing is complete, when a user asks whether a change meets its acceptance criteria, or when an independent judgment of requirement fidelity and repository standards is requested.
---

# Judge

## Select the action from the intent

Resolve approved scope, frozen candidate, evidence index, review mode and independence policy. Identify the reviewer and validate provenance before deriving a verdict.

| Intent / condition | Execute | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| Review a tested candidate for acceptance | Verify scope, candidate, evidence and required independence; review every mandatory criterion | Scoped verdict, actionable findings and uncertainties |
| Review requirement fidelity and repository standards | Assess requested behavior separately from documented quality standards | Separate requirement and standards findings with sources and corrective checks |
| Score a candidate | Apply the review mode and rubric agreed before implementation | Evidence-derived weighted score/coverage, or N/A in predefined small-task mode |
| Review a branch, diff or pull request without Test evidence | Bind its exact head commit as the frozen candidate; review it against stated criteria and standards; name the missing Test evidence | Findings labeled non-acceptance; indeterminate unless a confirmed defect requires correction; not merge approval |
| Evidence or required independence is missing | Record the exact gap; use indeterminate unless a known defect already requires correction | Specific prerequisite, not self-approval or an invented pass |

Execute the selected action through the workflow below and verify its result
before taking the next action. Loading this Skill is not authorization
for tracker writes, Git operations, installation or production effects.

## Workflow

A phase report is the result of this Skill, not a file to find before execution.
Collect its facts during work; deliver them inline by default at the delivery step.
Save a report only with an explicit destination and permission to write, following
the common output contract loaded at that step. Required evidence inputs and tracker
updates retain their own gates; an inline response does not replace task truth.

Apply contracts before their governed actions, even before the step that links them.
Read a reference only when it is absent, incomplete or outdated in the active context.
Reuse identical copies from another Skill. The same ID/version with different content
is a conflict, not proof of identity; resolve it before the affected action.
A loaded marker or earlier read does not prove availability. After compaction, a new
session or worker, reload missing required instructions. After workspace changes,
recheck applicability. Reused authorization guidance never renews a permission.
This is an agent instruction, not a runtime cache.

1. [ ] **Verify scope, authority and reviewer prerequisites**

   Apply [the requirements baseline](references/requirements-baseline.md) before
   defining or changing scope, criteria, checks or verification, and before running checks.
   Resolve the approved task baseline; retain verified Goals/Non-goals, FR/GWT and relevant
   quantified NFRs without inventing targets; keep missing requirements explicit.

   Apply [the authorization policy](references/authorization-policy.md) before
   resuming artifact claims or executing consequential actions; verify current
   permission for the intended action, not historical approval.

   Before creating or repairing task descriptions or acceptance criteria, verify
   current scope and write authority. Conditionally Load `agentic-development:task-authoring`
   using the host's available Skill-loading mechanism (not a shell command), with
   established goal, scope, criteria, native tracker context and current authority.
   Reuse its guidance when already available and current; do not load both routes
   normally. If the optional capability is unavailable, apply contained
   [ticket authoring](references/ticket-authoring.md) directly and report direct
   reading, not activation; do not retry loading or block routine work on its absence.
   For routine reads, claims, progress updates or closure, do not load task-authoring.
   Resume this caller after verified ticket readback or an explicit proposal/error;
   retain this phase's scope, ownership, review and evidence gates.

   If the repository uses Beads, apply [the Beads integration](references/beads-integration.md)
   before choosing work or mutating task state. Run `bd prime` only when Beads context is missing or stale;
   retain task ownership, readback and phase gates;
   evaluate commit suitability after each confirmed closure without inferring Git authority.

   Apply [the communication contract](references/communication-contract.md) before
   the first mutation and before preparing the first checkpoint or a Git/session transition,
   for ownership, transition, evidence and conditional UI reporting safeguards, not an
   up-front load of response templates. Apply these safeguards in standalone use too.
   Respond in the user's language. Verify tools and permissions; unavailable
   capabilities produce an explicit blocker, never simulated execution evidence.
   When acting as a delegated worker, use the coordinator's verified slice state; do not fabricate execution or acceptance.

   Before deriving a judgment, apply [the judgment rubric](references/judgment-rubric.md) unless
   an explicitly approved replacement rubric is supplied. Record its version.

   Require approved acceptance scope, frozen candidate identity, diff/ownership
   ledger, evidence index and known limitations. Recommend an independent context
   before judgment; announce the transition and prepare a handoff without an
   automatic commit. Identify reviewer/context and all required independence dimensions from the review policy.
   Require the plan-time independence decision; default US acceptance requires
   independent review. A new session alone is insufficient. If reviewing your own work in the
   same context, disclose limited self-review; never claim independence. If required
   independence is unavailable, the verdict is indeterminate unless a known blocker
   already justifies needs-correction.

2. [ ] **Bind the frozen candidate and review basis**

   Apply [candidate identity](references/candidate-identity.md) before planning checks,
   freezing or comparing inputs or reusing evidence; include staged, untracked and binary inputs
   and explicitly defined output-only exclusions.
   For exact-candidate proof, use the contained [capture/validate/compare CLI](scripts/candidate_identity.py) with the [scope example](references/candidate-scope.example.json); consult the [manifest schema](references/candidate-identity.schema.json) and [manifest example](references/candidate-identity.example.json) when preparing or validating its JSON. Follow the candidate procedure above; equality is not acceptance.

   Apply [the review policy](references/review-policy.md) before setting or reporting
   acceptance/review requirements, before implementation, and before proposing or agreeing
   acceptance, judging or closing a task/US. Independence and closure requirements are
   set at plan time, before implementation; a missing capability does not waive them.

   Match proofs to candidate/environment and scope. Inspect relevant code and
   actual test artifacts; do not accept builder summaries as sole proof.

3. [ ] **Review requirements and standards separately**

   Identify the requirement/specification and documented standards for the exact
   candidate. Report requirement fidelity (missing, incorrect or unauthorized behavior)
   separately from repository standards/maintainability. A passing standards review
   cannot compensate for implementing the wrong behavior. Missing specification or
   standard sources are disclosed, not invented. A pinned Git comparison is useful
   but must include relevant staged, dirty and untracked inputs in candidate identity.

   Treat code smells as labeled heuristics, not hard violations; project standards
   take precedence over generic taste. Do not repeat automated checks as unsupported
   manual findings. Use parallel read-only reviewers only when capabilities and
   independence requirements are satisfied; different sessions/models alone are not proof.

   Collect Requirement findings and Standards findings separately for the judgment
   report evidence section. Each finding needs criterion/source, location, observation,
   impact and minimal corrective check. Preserve the existing evidence/verdict/score/
   insights separation; no invented numeric score or acceptance from builder assertions.

   Review each mandatory acceptance criterion, risk-based security/regression,
   maintainability and operability. Missing evidence is unknown, not zero defects.
   For application-test evidence, challenge marginal detection value and independent
   oracles: mock self-validation, copied expected calculations, vague assertions for
   exact outcomes, success/error ambiguity and missing important error paths cannot
   support the claimed guarantee. Review rationalization decisions against preserved
   product coverage, not legacy volume; a green test count is not quality or acceptance.
   Ask whether a reader, without opening the implementation, can explain the rule each
   new test protects and give a concrete example; an unreadable test or a same-branch
   duplicate (an input-only variant that neither the code nor the specification
   distinguishes) is a non-blocking finding unless a criterion requires otherwise.
   Check observed failing counterexamples versus hypothetical faults and required
   end-to-end CI wall time versus aggregate/local durations. Missing measurements or
   discrimination stay explicit; do not infer CI acceptance from parallel local runs.
   Keep this review risk-scoped; no exhaustive new test/mutation campaign or candidate
   edits during Judge.
   Reproduce checks only when capabilities and permissions allow; do not mutate
   the candidate or repair code while judging.

   If specialist or parallel reviewers are used, verify actual invocation/completion status, source/candidate identity, result locators and required independence. Incomplete results remain provisional.

4. [ ] **Verify findings and derive the scoped verdict**

   For code review or specialist findings, read [finding verification](references/finding-verification.md)
   before publishing claims. Check surrounding context and reachable failure paths,
   separate observed from inferred evidence, justify severity by impact and consolidate
   duplicates. Keep mandatory defects and missing-evidence gates; a filter against
   unsupported findings is not permission to suppress a required acceptance failure.

   Record findings with severity, location, criterion, evidence, impact and
   corrective verification. Distinguish blocking defects from recommendations.

   Apply the plan-time review mode in the versioned rubric. In weighted mode,
   calculate criterion values, coverage and score from evidence, keeping unknowns
   null. In small-task mode report score not-applicable, without numeric grading.
   Neither mode can override a failed mandatory gate or waive independence.

   Accept only an exact candidate with every mandatory criterion evidenced and no
   blocking findings. Candidate changes invalidate affected judgment. Never silently
   relax criteria, retroactively redefine the rubric or approve your own human gate.

   **Result contract**

   Return one scoped verdict and a separate score state; PASS/FAIL labels belong to
   executed checks, not the acceptance verdict. Use these exact verdict values:

   | Verdict | Choose when |
   |---|---|
   | `accepted` | Every mandatory criterion is evidenced, no blocker remains and required independence is satisfied |
   | `needs-correction` | A confirmed defect or unmet mandatory criterion requires correction; known blockers take precedence over gaps |
   | `indeterminate` | Required evidence, capability, provenance or independence is missing, with no known blocker establishing correction |
   | `not-run` | No Judge review was executed; do not assign a score |

   Use the plan-time mode: `weighted` yields a 0–100 score only when every rubric
   criterion is assessed; unknowns leave the overall score null. `small-task` yields
   score N/A. A score never overrides a failed mandatory gate; a score below 100 is not
   by itself a failure. At step 6 emit the delivery contract's result block inside explanation,
   with reasons and evidence; do not create another outer report or runtime JSON.


5. [ ] **Collect judgment facts and the immediate prerequisite**

   Collect judgment report facts for inline delivery or an explicitly authorized
   saved report. Keep evidence, scoped verdict, rubric mode/score,
   insights (observed/inferred/to-verify), risks and unknowns separate; format the
   delivery only at the output gate below.
   Local acceptance is not real-provider approval.
   Collect verdict, review mode, rubric identity/version, score state/coverage,
   blockers and limitations for the result block; do not invent missing values.

   Collect checkpoint inputs: candidate, exact acceptance scope, open findings,
   immediate action and its prerequisite. Publish them only at the delivery gate;
   a proposed transition never authorizes closure or Iterate.

6. [ ] **Read delivery guidance and draft the phase response**

   After investigation and immediately before drafting any user-facing phase response (including blocked or unchanged results), apply [the common output contract](references/common-output.md) and [this phase's delivery contract](references/requirements-output.md); apply their checklists and selected delivery form (compact when eligible, otherwise five-section report). Keep the canonical phase artifact within that report. Before drafting a proposed, performed, failed or externally observed commit report, apply [the commit report](references/commit-report.md). Before drafting a planned session end, explicit wrap-up or recommended context transition report, apply [the session report](references/session-report.md). Combine overlapping reports without duplication.

   After reading delivery guidance, draft the actual handoff fenced YAML state card and copy-ready restart prompt; distinguish proposed from performed actions.

7. [ ] **Execute the handoff or stop**

   Execute the next phase only when it belongs to the user's requested workflow and
   current scope/permissions cover its actions. For a phase-only request, return the
   phase result and proposed handoff, then stop; do not expand the request by loading
   or executing a new phase. If continuing is authorized, apply the routes below.

   Select exactly one route from the verdict; record its owner, prerequisite and expected result.

   | Verdict | Immediate action | Required inputs / result |
   |---|---|---|
   | `accepted` | Return the exact accepted scope to the coordinator/user; no implicit closure, commit, push, merge or release | Candidate ID, criterion evidence, score state and limits; any publication/closure needs separate authority |
   | `needs-correction` | If continuation is authorized, Load `agentic-development:iterate`; otherwise return the proposed correction handoff and stop | Confirmed finding IDs, scoped verdict, candidate, evidence, minimal corrective checks and current correction budget; repair then Test and Judge the changed candidate |
   | `indeterminate` | Resolve the named proof/capability/provenance/independence gap; no speculative code repair | Name missing input and supplier; route missing checks to Test only when authorized, or request the required reviewer/access. Re-run Judge when prerequisites are satisfied; a newly confirmed defect changes the route to needs-correction. A second indeterminate verdict on the same candidate for the same gap stops and returns the blocker to the user instead of another Test round |
   | `not-run` | Execute Judge only if requested and its prerequisites are available; otherwise return its prerequisite checklist and stop | Approved scope, frozen candidate, evidence index, plan-time mode and reviewer/independence; first review produces a verdict, not an assumed failure or acceptance |

   needs-correction means change a confirmed defective candidate; indeterminate means
   establish whether it can be judged. Keep them distinct because their actions differ.
   Missing permission blocks the selected action, not permission to substitute another route.

   Use the host's available Skill-loading mechanism; these identifiers are not shell
   commands. If loading is unavailable, read the selected bundled SKILL.md and its
   required contained references, and report direct reading rather than activation.
   Pass a copy-ready handoff if execution cannot continue in this context. State the
   specific missing input, permission or capability, who can supply it when known,
   and the next executable action. Do not merely say "blocked" or "continue later".

# slice-acceptance — rubric v1.1.0

Contract ID: agentic-development/judgment-rubric
Contract version: 1.1.0

Freeze this default rubric before implementation, or record the approved
replacement identifier/version. Score is a structured assessment, not a
probability of correctness. Assess only the explicitly agreed acceptance scope.

| Criterion | Weight | Required basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Functional acceptance | 40 | Each approved functional criterion mapped to evidence |
| Verification quality | 25 | Relevant tests, negative paths, environment and candidate identity |
| Safety and regression | 20 | Risk-based security, data integrity and regression checks |
| Maintainability | 10 | Diff, interfaces, local conventions and avoidable complexity |
| Operability and handoff | 5 | Run prerequisites, limitations and reproducible next steps |

Per criterion: 0 unmet, 1 materially incomplete, 2 partial, 3 meets the agreed
scope, 4 exceeds it with concrete evidence. Weighted score = sum(weight * value/4)
on a 0–100 scale. Report unknown criteria as null. For partial scoring report
only earned/assessed weight and assessment coverage; do not normalize it into
an apparently complete overall score. Overall score remains null if any
criterion is unknown. Omit an irrelevant criterion only through an explicitly
approved versioned rubric amendment, not silently during grading.

Accepted: every mandatory acceptance criterion has adequate evidence and no
blocking finding remains. Needs-correction: a known defect or unmet mandatory
criterion exists. Indeterminate: evidence, capability, provenance or required
independence is missing. Known blockers take precedence over missing evidence.
Not-run: no judge was executed. A high score never overrides these gates.

For each finding record ID, severity, criterion, file/location, evidence,
impact, remediation and verification needed. Distinguish blocking findings from
nonblocking recommendations. Report reviewer identity/context and whether
review was independent, limited self-review or not executed.

## Explicit small-task mode

Select the mode before implementation, in the plan or verified scope. For a narrow local
or authoring task whose decision does not benefit from numerical grading, use
small-task mode: mandatory criteria, observed checks, findings, limitations and
scoped verdict; score and numerical coverage are not-applicable. No rubric
amendment is needed for this predefined mode. Never switch modes after seeing a
failure to hide it. A numeric score already required by the user/approved plan
remains required unless that authority approves the change.

Small-task mode does not waive exact-candidate acceptance, any mandatory proof,
independence, closure authority or parent/release gates. Weighted mode remains
the default for feature/release slices and for explicit numerical requests.

## Interpreting conformity

Five criteria rated 3 earn 40*3/4 + 25*3/4 + 20*3/4 + 10*3/4 + 5*3/4 = 75/100.
This means meets the agreed scope, not a 75 percent chance of correctness or
a failed acceptance gate. A 4 requires concrete evidence of exceeding scope,
not unauthorized extra work. Do not expand scope just to chase 100.

If the first four criteria are 3 and operability (weight 5) is unknown, earned
points are 71.25 against assessed weight 95; coverage is 95 percent and overall
score is null. Never normalize this partial result to a complete overall score.
Mandatory missing proof or required independence still prevents acceptance.
Apply review-policy.md for independence/closure; rubric scoring grants no authority.
# Verify findings before publishing

Read when judging code changes or assessing a specialist reviewer finding. It refines evidence quality; it does not replace the acceptance criteria, rubric or independence policy.

## Check the claim

1. Match location and source version to the frozen candidate. Read surrounding context, callers and relevant contracts before interpreting an isolated line. Check reachability and the preconditions under which the alleged failure can occur. Inspect protective validation or error propagation before claiming it is absent.
2. Identify the requirement or documented standard affected. State the concrete expected versus actual outcome and impact. Generic taste, arbitrary function-size thresholds and speculative refactors are not defects without a relevant source or demonstrated failure.
3. Prefer a minimal permitted reproduction at the public seam. Otherwise record a source-grounded argument, assumptions and what was not reproduced. Mark evidence observed, inferred or unknown; source inspection may establish a defect, but must not be mislabeled as executed behavior. Do not repair the candidate or execute unapproved side effects.
4. Check whether an automated result or another finding already covers the same root cause. Consolidate duplicate findings while preserving distinct impacts and criterion links; never inflate the count by restating the same issue.

## Qualify severity and uncertainty

Assign severity from demonstrated impact, exposure/reachability and affected scope using the agreed project policy. Do not invent confidence percentages or promote style preferences to security failures. Missing context/access means an explicit evidence gap, not a clean result. Suspicious but unconfirmed claims belong in uncertainties with the smallest verification prerequisite, not in a list of confirmed defects.

Do not discard a known mandatory acceptance failure because it is small, inconvenient, not reproduced dynamically, or below a generic review threshold. Conversely, an unsupported claim is not a known blocker. If mandatory evidence or required independence is missing, retain the existing indeterminate gate unless an established defect requires needs-correction.

## Publish an actionable finding

Record ID, requirement/standard source, exact location, preconditions, evidence type and locator, expected/actual result, impact, justified severity, blocking versus recommendation status and minimal corrective verification. Keep requirement and standards findings separate, and preserve the judgment evidence/verdict/score distinction. Return findings to Judge/coordinator; a specialist review is not an independent acceptance decision by itself.

## Review scenarios

- A launcher appears to suppress failure: inspect child status and wrapper propagation; reproduce at the public CLI when permitted before claiming observed success masking.
- A long function works and violates no project standard: omit a taste-only defect; record a recommendation only if its concrete maintenance benefit is justified.
- Missing access prevents checking a reported security path: retain the uncertainty and next probe without inventing a confirmed vulnerability or accepting a mandatory unverified criterion.
# Judgment independence and closure v1.0.0

Contract ID: agentic-development/review-policy
Contract version: 1.0.0

## Plan-time choice

Before implementation, record required reviewer independence, acceptance scope,
closure authority and verification proportional to risk. Default: independent
review is required for US acceptance and release recommendations. A current user
or active trusted project policy may explicitly waive independence for a defined
small/local slice; record that source and scope. A builder's saved plan or an
absence of reviewer tools is not a waiver. Do not widen the slice or lower its
mandatory evidence to make it easier to close.

A narrow authoring/test task can complete under its own documented quality gates
without claiming parent US acceptance or release approval. Mark its self-review
as limited and preserve open independent/real validation tasks. This is not a
waiver of an existing task criterion requiring independent review.

## Declare independence dimensions

Record reviewer identity/context, participation in construction, inherited
context, exposure to builder conclusions or expected verdict, direct access to
frozen candidate and raw evidence, and write permissions. Different session IDs
or different models alone do not prove independence. Give a reviewer criteria,
necessary factual context, candidate and evidence; do not inject the builder's
private reasoning or desired verdict. Exposure to builder conclusions must be
disclosed as a limit. Reviewers must not repair or mutate the candidate.

## Verdict and closure gates

If independence is required and unavailable, use indeterminate unless a known
blocking defect already establishes needs-correction. Full tests or a high score
do not compensate. If an explicit scoped waiver permits limited self-review,
label the verdict limited, cite the waiver and keep broader US/release gates open.
No US/parent issue closure from self-review without a current explicit grant
covering that closure, and never contrary to a required independence gate.

Acceptance needs all mandatory scope criteria evidenced for the exact candidate
with no blockers. Score is separate and cannot authorize closure. A tracker
update is a separate permitted action: verify authority and actual outcome.
Only the designated owner closes the completed issue's scope; do not close a
shared parent because one subtask finished. Human approval is never self-granted.
# Candidate identity v1.4.0

Contract ID: agentic-development/candidate-identity
Contract version: 1.4.0

Use before planning checks, freezing a candidate or reusing evidence. Choose the
path matching the purpose; source reading alone is not an acceptance check.

## Source-only observation

Record inspected paths/sections, revision or file identity, current dirty state and
provenance limits. For bounded source reading, no capture CLI or full manifest is
required. Do not imply executed behavior, complete input coverage or exact-candidate
acceptance from a revision/hash. Refresh affected conclusions when inputs change.
Preliminary executed checks use A; exact-candidate acceptance or proof reuse uses B.
Reusing a cited observation with verified freshness does not turn it into B proof.

## A. Run a preliminary check

1. Record the command, relevant input paths, environment and observed exit/result.
2. Label provenance limited; no full manifest is required for a smoke check.
3. Before using this result for exact-candidate acceptance or proof reuse, follow B
   and rerun the checks. Never retroactively relabel the preliminary result.

## B. Bind checks to an exact candidate

1. Verify Python >=3.10; Git workspaces also require the Git CLI and their worktree
   root. Resolve this Skill's directory as `SKILL_DIR`; the shell cwd is not that directory.
2. Copy the bundled scope example to an authorized location outside the inputs.
   Replace include paths, criteria identity and non-secret environment values.
   Use sorted unique root-relative paths (directories recurse, including ignored
   and untracked files). Include code, tests, fixtures, configuration, lockfiles,
   consumed reports, applicable instructions and the verification tool itself.
   Review task dependencies: the tool cannot discover omitted inputs or secrets.
3. Keep exclusions narrow: each has a path and reason, approved before checks,
   and must be output-only, never consumed. Do not exclude user work merely because
   it is dirty/untracked. External inputs require an authorized local snapshot in
   scope or remain BLOCKED/UNKNOWN. Do not copy sensitive data without permission.
4. Set SKILL_DIR, PROJECT_ROOT and an authorized EVIDENCE_DIR outside the captured
   inputs. Prepare the scope file, then capture before execution:

~~~sh
cp "$SKILL_DIR/references/candidate-scope.example.json" "$EVIDENCE_DIR/scope.json"
# Edit scope.json with verified paths, environment and criteria before capture.
python3 -B "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/candidate_identity.py" capture \
  --root "$PROJECT_ROOT" --scope "$EVIDENCE_DIR/scope.json" > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/before.json"
~~~

5. Require exit 0 and a manifest with candidate_id. Record commands, actual results,
   environment and approved criteria against that ID; execute the scoped checks.
6. Capture again with the same root/scope and compare:

~~~sh
python3 -B "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/candidate_identity.py" capture \
  --root "$PROJECT_ROOT" --scope "$EVIDENCE_DIR/scope.json" > "$EVIDENCE_DIR/after.json"
python3 -B "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/candidate_identity.py" compare \
  "$EVIDENCE_DIR/before.json" "$EVIDENCE_DIR/after.json"
~~~

7. Exit 0 / SAME: inputs match, not acceptance. Exit 1 / DIFFERENT: inspect changes

+## Same branch is not a new test
+
+Before adding a test that differs from a neighbour only in an input value, confirm
+that the production code or the specification distinguishes that value. A
+passthrough field, or one guard rejecting every disallowed enum value, means the
+existing test already covers it: add the value to that test's example data only
+when it documents the rule, not as another test.
+
+Add the case when the code branches on the value, when the specification names it
+as a distinct boundary, error or incident, or when a distinct environment can
+expose a different fault. If the specification distinguishes a value that the code
+does not, write that test: its failure reveals a gap, not a duplicate.
+
+Every redundant test costs CI time and the tokens an agent spends reading it later.
+During an authorized rationalization, look for same-branch variants and
+cross-file duplicates of the same guarantee, then apply the merge or remove
+decision below with the retained check named.
+
+## Write tests as living documentation
+
+A reader who does not know the code should learn from the tests what the software
+must do, by reading concrete examples that run.
+
+| Part | What it must tell the reader |
+|---|---|
+| Name | The name states the rule: `test_site_without_approval_cannot_be_published`, not `test_publish_returns_409`. |
+| Given | Only the conditions that matter. Name fixtures in domain terms; add those that rule out other causes, so the reader sees which condition decides the outcome. |
+| When | Perform one action, by a user or the system. |
+| Then | The expected outcome and, when the rule depends on them, its effects, including state left unchanged by a refusal. |
+| Set of cases | The set of cases bounds the rule: at least one allowed and one refused example, plus each case the specification distinguishes. |

+def test_site_without_approval_cannot_be_published(
+    ready_site_without_approval,
+    authorized_publisher,
+):
+    site = ready_site_without_approval
+
+    with pytest.raises(ApprovalRequired):
+        site.publish(by=authorized_publisher)
+
+    assert site.status == SiteStatus.READY
+~~~
+
+`authorized_publisher` establishes that permissions suffice, so the refusal can
+only come from the missing approval. The last assertion states a second guarantee
+of the same scenario: the refusal leaves the site unchanged.
+
+- Choose the level by the guarantee. A domain rule is asserted on domain outcomes.
+  A public API contract can assert the HTTP status and error code clients rely on,
+  for example `409` with an approval-required code.
+- Keep the criterion ID in a docstring or marker unless the project convention puts
+  it elsewhere; the name stays readable as the rule.
+- A green test confirms that the written scenario works. Review still checks that
+  the scenario still expresses the intended rule; when a rule changes on purpose,
+  review the behavior change and its examples together.
+- Review question: **without opening the implementation, can I explain the rule
+  this test protects and give a concrete example of what must happen?** A no is a
+  readability finding.

# Product guarantees and test value v1.0.0

Contract ID: agentic-development/test-value
Contract version: 1.0.0

Apply when writing, selecting or reviewing application tests, or analyzing a suite
for rationalization. This is not permission to edit tests or the frozen candidate.
Implement writes tests within an authorized task; Test diagnoses and proposes
changes; authorized corrections go through Iterate and Implement, then Test checks
the changed candidate.

## Contents

- [Select evidence, not volume](#select-evidence-not-volume)
- [Same branch is not a new test](#same-branch-is-not-a-new-test)
- [Write tests as living documentation](#write-tests-as-living-documentation)
- [Challenge the oracle before counting a pass](#challenge-the-oracle-before-counting-a-pass)
- [Rationalize within authority](#rationalize-within-authority)
- [Measure the mandatory path honestly](#measure-the-mandatory-path-honestly)
- [Source and applicability](#source-and-applicability)

## Select evidence, not volume

1. Start from the approved product guarantees and important user journeys, not
   existing test files or implementation structure. Include relevant errors,
   cancellation, boundaries, security and observed incidents. Do not invent every
   imaginable input combination. Missing expected behavior is a requirements gap.
2. For each selected test or coherent test family answer:
   **Which incorrect observable product behavior does this detect that the other
   selected checks do not already detect?** Record the guarantee/criterion ID,
   concrete fault, independent oracle, public seam and evidence level. A distinct
   environment or boundary can justify overlap; assertion/file count cannot.
3. Choose the cheapest valid check at that seam. Use direct deterministic cases
   for business-rule variations; keep a representative integration for actual
   wiring and a small set of operational journeys for required system guarantees.
   Do not replace a required integration, installed-package, real-provider or UI
   observation with a cheaper mock that cannot expose the same fault.
4. Add a case only for a distinct risk, boundary, incident or confidence question.
   Existing tests are not a preservation obligation. There is not a fixed test-count ceiling
   or minimum: a large suite can be justified, a small green suite can be worthless.
   Do not target an arbitrary reduction percentage, coverage percentage or number.

A compact selection matrix is enough; group genuinely equivalent cases rather
than produce an audit document per test. For a requested whole-suite audit,
account for every test/family; an uninspected subset stays unknown, not useless.

| Guarantee / source | Incorrect behavior | Oracle / seam / level | Marginal detection value | Cost / required lane |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approved criterion ID | Concrete externally wrong result | Independent expected result, actual subject | Distinct fault or justified overlap | Measured or unknown; local/required CI/optional |

## Same branch is not a new test

Before adding a test that differs from a neighbour only in an input value, confirm
that the production code or the specification distinguishes that value. A
passthrough field, or one guard rejecting every disallowed enum value, means the
existing test already covers it: add the value to that test's example data only
when it documents the rule, not as another test.

Add the case when the code branches on the value, when the specification names it
as a distinct boundary, error or incident, or when a distinct environment can
expose a different fault. If the specification distinguishes a value that the code
does not, write that test: its failure reveals a gap, not a duplicate.

Every redundant test costs CI time and the tokens an agent spends reading it later.
During an authorized rationalization, look for same-branch variants and
cross-file duplicates of the same guarantee, then apply the merge or remove
decision below with the retained check named.

## Write tests as living documentation

A reader who does not know the code should learn from the tests what the software
must do, by reading concrete examples that run.

| Part | What it must tell the reader |
|---|---|
| Name | The name states the rule: `test_site_without_approval_cannot_be_published`, not `test_publish_returns_409`. |
| Given | Only the conditions that matter. Name fixtures in domain terms; add those that rule out other causes, so the reader sees which condition decides the outcome. |
| When | Perform one action, by a user or the system. |
| Then | The expected outcome and, when the rule depends on them, its effects, including state left unchanged by a refusal. |
| Set of cases | The set of cases bounds the rule: at least one allowed and one refused example, plus each case the specification distinguishes. |

~~~python
def test_site_without_approval_cannot_be_published(
    ready_site_without_approval,
    authorized_publisher,
):
    site = ready_site_without_approval

    with pytest.raises(ApprovalRequired):
        site.publish(by=authorized_publisher)

    assert site.status == SiteStatus.READY
~~~

`authorized_publisher` establishes that permissions suffice, so the refusal can
only come from the missing approval. The last assertion states a second guarantee
of the same scenario: the refusal leaves the site unchanged.

- Choose the level by the guarantee. A domain rule is asserted on domain outcomes.
  A public API contract can assert the HTTP status and error code clients rely on,
  for example `409` with an approval-required code.
- Keep the criterion ID in a docstring or marker unless the project convention puts
  it elsewhere; the name stays readable as the rule.
- A green test confirms that the written scenario works. Review still checks that
  the scenario still expresses the intended rule; when a rule changes on purpose,
  review the behavior change and its examples together.
- Review question: **without opening the implementation, can I explain the rule
  this test protects and give a concrete example of what must happen?** A no is a
  readability finding.

## Challenge the oracle before counting a pass

- Exercise the actual subject. A test that only calculates or asserts its own
  setup is a tautology; copied production logic is not an independent oracle.
  Use specification examples, known exact values or independently justified
  properties. A test-only reimplementation of the subject proves nothing about it.
- A mock controls an external dependency, not the behavior being verified.
  Returning the mock's value and asserting that same value is insufficient unless
  a distinct product contract is discriminated (for example selecting the correct
  customer's ID, forwarding a mandated parameter, or translating a dependency error).
  Do not ban mocks or contractually meaningful interaction assertions wholesale.
- When the contract determines an exact outcome, assert it, including important
  persisted effects or absence of forbidden effects. Non-null, truthy, nonnegative
  or shape-only checks cannot substitute for the known result. Tolerances or
  property assertions need a contract-based justification, not vague correctness.
- Specify one expected outcome per input/state. Do not accept success or error
  interchangeably, catch failures to pass, silently skip missing prerequisites,
  or branch on the observed result to choose whichever assertion passes. Assert
  the success and important error paths separately with deterministic conditions.
- Check discrimination with a symptom-specific failing reproduction or a bounded
  counterexample/mutation at the real seam when authorized: wrong exact value,
  inverted decision, missing effect or swallowed error must make the relevant
  test fail. Keep probes isolated, restore the candidate, and never mutate the
  frozen candidate during Test. An existing pre-fix red can provide this evidence;
  do not mandate an exhaustive mutation campaign for every test. Without execution,
  label the fault hypothetical and discrimination unverified. Static red/green
  establishes source conformance, not application or agent behavior.

## Rationalize within authority

For an authorized suite rationalization, inspect assertions, setup and observed
cost hotspots before optimizing scheduling. Profile slow families and repeated
campaign setup first, not just cheap individual assertions. If no timings exist,
record unknown cost and propose the smallest useful measurement.

| Decision | Use when | Evidence needed |
|---|---|---|
| retain | Distinct product fault, security boundary, incident regression or required environment | Criterion, discriminating oracle and unique risk or justified overlap |
| merge | Checks duplicate the same guarantee or expensive setup | Representative integration plus cheap direct cases; preserve distinct faults |
| remove | Test validates only setup/internal detail or duplicates another check without distinct value | No unique product guarantee lost; identify retained coverage or explain irrelevance |
| replace | Guarantee matters but current test cannot expose its fault or is unnecessarily expensive | Better observable seam/oracle and relevant red-capable regression |

Record test/family, decision, rationale, guarantee lost or preserved, replacement
or retained check, discrimination evidence, cost before/after (or UNKNOWN), and
actual or proposed status. Removal/fusion is allowed within approved scope; do not
weaken product acceptance or discard meaningful incidents to obtain green or faster
results. Missing required coverage remains open until a valid replacement passes.
Preserve unrelated work and keep the old evidence's candidate identity intact.

Repeated costly end-to-end/provider/evaluation campaigns need a distinct risk or
confidence question, workload/sample justification, budget and stop rule. Prefer
one representative wiring journey and inexpensive rule cases when they expose
the same faults. Nondeterministic confidence requirements can justify repetition;
name the uncertainty being measured. Stop adding/running checks when selected
mandatory guarantees and scoped risk questions have adequate evidence, or stop
with explicit gaps when prerequisites/budget fail. Green count is not a stop rule.

## Measure the mandatory path honestly

Distinguish:
- individual and summed test durations: hotspots, often not end-to-end elapsed time;
- aggregate runner/compute time and costly service calls: total execution cost;
- required CI wall time: end-to-end mandatory workflow path, including checkout,
  dependency setup, build, tests, artifacts and required job dependencies/joins.

For CI claims identify the candidate, workflow/required jobs, runner environment,
parallelism/cache state, measurement start/end and observation window/runs. State
whether queue time is included. Compare only to an approved target and like-for-like
baseline; a local grouped run or summed timings do not prove the complete CI path.
Parallelism can reduce waiting without reducing aggregate work or improving test
value. Classify optional lanes explicitly; moving a required guarantee off the
mandatory path needs scoped approval, not an unreported speed optimization.
Unavailable CI measurement is UNKNOWN/NOT RUN, never an extrapolated pass. Targets
for downstream applications stay unresolved until their workload and approval are known.

At delivery carry the selection/decision matrix, defects actually detected with
reproduction evidence versus hypothetical faults, retained guarantees, open gaps,
and mandatory-path wall time versus aggregate cost. Test count is secondary context,
not evidence of confidence, rationalization or acceptance.

## Source and applicability

Michael Bromley, [The Problem With Your AI Tests](https://www.michaelbromley.co.uk/blog/the-problem-with-your-ai-tests/),
7 September 2026 (consulted 28 October 2026), describes tautologies, weak assertions,

# Product guarantees and test value v1.0.0

Contract ID: agentic-development/test-value
Contract version: 1.0.0

Apply when writing, selecting or reviewing application tests, or analyzing a suite
for rationalization. This is not permission to edit tests or the frozen candidate.
Implement writes tests within an authorized task; Test diagnoses and proposes
changes; authorized corrections go through Iterate and Implement, then Test checks
the changed candidate.

## Contents

- [Select evidence, not volume](#select-evidence-not-volume)
- [Same branch is not a new test](#same-branch-is-not-a-new-test)
- [Write tests as living documentation](#write-tests-as-living-documentation)
- [Challenge the oracle before counting a pass](#challenge-the-oracle-before-counting-a-pass)
- [Rationalize within authority](#rationalize-within-authority)
- [Measure the mandatory path honestly](#measure-the-mandatory-path-honestly)
- [Source and applicability](#source-and-applicability)

## Select evidence, not volume

1. Start from the approved product guarantees and important user journeys, not
   existing test files or implementation structure. Include relevant errors,
   cancellation, boundaries, security and observed incidents. Do not invent every
   imaginable input combination. Missing expected behavior is a requirements gap.
2. For each selected test or coherent test family answer:
   **Which incorrect observable product behavior does this detect that the other
   selected checks do not already detect?** Record the guarantee/criterion ID,
   concrete fault, independent oracle, public seam and evidence level. A distinct
   environment or boundary can justify overlap; assertion/file count cannot.
3. Choose the cheapest valid check at that seam. Use direct deterministic cases
   for business-rule variations; keep a representative integration for actual
   wiring and a small set of operational journeys for required system guarantees.
   Do not replace a required integration, installed-package, real-provider or UI
   observation with a cheaper mock that cannot expose the same fault.
4. Add a case only for a distinct risk, boundary, incident or confidence question.
   Existing tests are not a preservation obligation. There is not a fixed test-count ceiling
   or minimum: a large suite can be justified, a small green suite can be worthless.
   Do not target an arbitrary reduction percentage, coverage percentage or number.

A compact selection matrix is enough; group genuinely equivalent cases rather
than produce an audit document per test. For a requested whole-suite audit,
account for every test/family; an uninspected subset stays unknown, not useless.

| Guarantee / source | Incorrect behavior | Oracle / seam / level | Marginal detection value | Cost / required lane |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approved criterion ID | Concrete externally wrong result | Independent expected result, actual subject | Distinct fault or justified overlap | Measured or unknown; local/required CI/optional |

## Same branch is not a new test

Before adding a test that differs from a neighbour only in an input value, confirm
that the production code or the specification distinguishes that value. A
passthrough field, or one guard rejecting every disallowed enum value, means the
existing test already covers it: add the value to that test's example data only
when it documents the rule, not as another test.

Add the case when the code branches on the value, when the specification names it
as a distinct boundary, error or incident, or when a distinct environment can
expose a different fault. If the specification distinguishes a value that the code
does not, write that test: its failure reveals a gap, not a duplicate.

Every redundant test costs CI time and the tokens an agent spends reading it later.
During an authorized rationalization, look for same-branch variants and
cross-file duplicates of the same guarantee, then apply the merge or remove
decision below with the retained check named.

## Write tests as living documentation

A reader who does not know the code should learn from the tests what the software
must do, by reading concrete examples that run.

| Part | What it must tell the reader |
|---|---|
| Name | The name states the rule: `test_site_without_approval_cannot_be_published`, not `test_publish_returns_409`. |
| Given | Only the conditions that matter. Name fixtures in domain terms; add those that rule out other causes, so the reader sees which condition decides the outcome. |
| When | Perform one action, by a user or the system. |
| Then | The expected outcome and, when the rule depends on them, its effects, including state left unchanged by a refusal. |
| Set of cases | The set of cases bounds the rule: at least one allowed and one refused example, plus each case the specification distinguishes. |

~~~python
def test_site_without_approval_cannot_be_published(
    ready_site_without_approval,
    authorized_publisher,
):
    site = ready_site_without_approval

    with pytest.raises(ApprovalRequired):
        site.publish(by=authorized_publisher)

    assert site.status == SiteStatus.READY
~~~

`authorized_publisher` establishes that permissions suffice, so the refusal can
only come from the missing approval. The last assertion states a second guarantee
of the same scenario: the refusal leaves the site unchanged.

- Choose the level by the guarantee. A domain rule is asserted on domain outcomes.
  A public API contract can assert the HTTP status and error code clients rely on,
  for example `409` with an approval-required code.
- Keep the criterion ID in a docstring or marker unless the project convention puts
  it elsewhere; the name stays readable as the rule.
- A green test confirms that the written scenario works. Review still checks that
  the scenario still expresses the intended rule; when a rule changes on purpose,
  review the behavior change and its examples together.
- Review question: **without opening the implementation, can I explain the rule
  this test protects and give a concrete example of what must happen?** A no is a
  readability finding.

## Challenge the oracle before counting a pass

- Exercise the actual subject. A test that only calculates or asserts its own
  setup is a tautology; copied production logic is not an independent oracle.
  Use specification examples, known exact values or independently justified
  properties. A test-only reimplementation of the subject proves nothing about it.
- A mock controls an external dependency, not the behavior being verified.
  Returning the mock's value and asserting that same value is insufficient unless
  a distinct product contract is discriminated (for example selecting the correct
  customer's ID, forwarding a mandated parameter, or translating a dependency error).
  Do not ban mocks or contractually meaningful interaction assertions wholesale.
- When the contract determines an exact outcome, assert it, including important
  persisted effects or absence of forbidden effects. Non-null, truthy, nonnegative
  or shape-only checks cannot substitute for the known result. Tolerances or
  property assertions need a contract-based justification, not vague correctness.
- Specify one expected outcome per input/state. Do not accept success or error
  interchangeably, catch failures to pass, silently skip missing prerequisites,
  or branch on the observed result to choose whichever assertion passes. Assert
  the success and important error paths separately with deterministic conditions.
- Check discrimination with a symptom-specific failing reproduction or a bounded
  counterexample/mutation at the real seam when authorized: wrong exact value,
  inverted decision, missing effect or swallowed error must make the relevant
  test fail. Keep probes isolated, restore the candidate, and never mutate the
  frozen candidate during Test. An existing pre-fix red can provide this evidence;
  do not mandate an exhaustive mutation campaign for every test. Without execution,
  label the fault hypothetical and discrimination unverified. Static red/green
  establishes source conformance, not application or agent behavior.

## Rationalize within authority

For an authorized suite rationalization, inspect assertions, setup and observed
cost hotspots before optimizing scheduling. Profile slow families and repeated
campaign setup first, not just cheap individual assertions. If no timings exist,
record unknown cost and propose the smallest useful measurement.

| Decision | Use when | Evidence needed |
|---|---|---|
| retain | Distinct product fault, security boundary, incident regression or required environment | Criterion, discriminating oracle and unique risk or justified overlap |
| merge | Checks duplicate the same guarantee or expensive setup | Representative integration plus cheap direct cases; preserve distinct faults |
| remove | Test validates only setup/internal detail or duplicates another check without distinct value | No unique product guarantee lost; identify retained coverage or explain irrelevance |
| replace | Guarantee matters but current test cannot expose its fault or is unnecessarily expensive | Better observable seam/oracle and relevant red-capable regression |

Record test/family, decision, rationale, guarantee lost or preserved, replacement
or retained check, discrimination evidence, cost before/after (or UNKNOWN), and
actual or proposed status. Removal/fusion is allowed within approved scope; do not
weaken product acceptance or discard meaningful incidents to obtain green or faster
results. Missing required coverage remains open until a valid replacement passes.
Preserve unrelated work and keep the old evidence's candidate identity intact.

Repeated costly end-to-end/provider/evaluation campaigns need a distinct risk or
confidence question, workload/sample justification, budget and stop rule. Prefer
one representative wiring journey and inexpensive rule cases when they expose
the same faults. Nondeterministic confidence requirements can justify repetition;
name the uncertainty being measured. Stop adding/running checks when selected
mandatory guarantees and scoped risk questions have adequate evidence, or stop
with explicit gaps when prerequisites/budget fail. Green count is not a stop rule.

## Measure the mandatory path honestly

Distinguish:
- individual and summed test durations: hotspots, often not end-to-end elapsed time;
- aggregate runner/compute time and costly service calls: total execution cost;
- required CI wall time: end-to-end mandatory workflow path, including checkout,
  dependency setup, build, tests, artifacts and required job dependencies/joins.

For CI claims identify the candidate, workflow/required jobs, runner environment,
parallelism/cache state, measurement start/end and observation window/runs. State
whether queue time is included. Compare only to an approved target and like-for-like
baseline; a local grouped run or summed timings do not prove the complete CI path.
Parallelism can reduce waiting without reducing aggregate work or improving test
value. Classify optional lanes explicitly; moving a required guarantee off the
mandatory path needs scoped approval, not an unreported speed optimization.
Unavailable CI measurement is UNKNOWN/NOT RUN, never an extrapolated pass. Targets
for downstream applications stay unresolved until their workload and approval are known.

At delivery carry the selection/decision matrix, defects actually detected with
reproduction evidence versus hypothetical faults, retained guarantees, open gaps,
and mandatory-path wall time versus aggregate cost. Test count is secondary context,
not evidence of confidence, rationalization or acceptance.

## Source and applicability

Michael Bromley, [The Problem With Your AI Tests](https://www.michaelbromley.co.uk/blog/the-problem-with-your-ai-tests/),
7 September 2026 (consulted 28 October 2026), describes tautologies, weak assertions,
missing edge cases, conditional pass logic and implementation-mirroring setup.
Its large suite and reported review findings are the author's observations, not
benchmarks or efficacy evidence for this Skill. The selection, rationalization
and CI-cost procedure above also incorporates the user's disproportionate-suite
feedback; historical counts and timings are not portable acceptance targets.

Ido Shamun, "Reducing redundant test bloat generated by AI coding agents", daily.dev
(text supplied by the user, consulted 19 November 2026), describes agents adding
repetitive coverage-driven tests and proposes the same-branch rule above; its
reported removals are the author's observations, not benchmarks. The living
documentation section incorporates the user's feedback of the same date.
